hypothesis: The sign-cloudinary endpoint accepts paramsToSign from the client body without validating folder whitelists, potentially allowing an attacker to generate signatures for arbitrary folders outside tabidachi_capsules or ryan_travel.

If the unlock determination relies on client-provided timestamps or local date strings without strictly converting destination end_date to UTC midnight, users in earlier timezones or with manipulated clock headers could prematurely unlock trip capsules.

When a trip collaborator queries capsule entries prior to trip completion, if the serialization layer or database query fails to redact content and photo_url for non-authors, confidential entries will leak to collaborators via DevTools.

If the capsule submission schema accepts arbitrary photo_url strings without strictly asserting the https://res.cloudinary.com domain, attackers could inject internal IP addresses or javascript URI schemes leading to SSRF or XSS.
